title: How does an electric eel make electricity?
hook: A species described in 2019 delivered an 860-volt shock.
summary: Electric eels have organs built from stacked cells that produce discharges; a species described in 2019 reached 860 volts.

cardBlocks.text: The electric eel is a fish with organs that can generate an electric charge. These organs are made of electrocytes, cells derived from muscle and arranged in stacks along the body. With them, the fish delivers strong shocks to defend itself and catch prey, and weak pulses to sense hidden prey and communicate.

For a long time, all electric eels were thought to be one species. In 2019, a study in the journal Nature Communications showed there are three. One of the new ones, Electrophorus voltai, produced an 860-volt discharge, the record among known animals. The previous maximum on record was 650 volts.
Electric eels make electricity with stacks of special cells; a species described in 2019 reached 860 volts.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Despite the name, electric eels are not closely related to true eels.
Their shocks were first studied in 1775, and that work contributed to the invention of the electric battery in 1800.

Besides E. voltai, there is E. electricus, at 650 volts, and E. varii, with discharges between 151 and 572 volts. The researchers think the amount of salts dissolved in each one’s water may explain the difference.
